claims.statement: EU rules require public charging operators to make static and dynamic data, including operational status and availability, accessible through APIs.
The implementing rules require dynamic charging data to update rapidly and impose source data-quality controls.

contrary_evidence: Public operational-status data are not themselves proof that a private SLA was breached or that a credit is owed.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Resolved claims produce model- and operator-specific failure, exclusion and credit benchmarks
fingerprint.customer: Fleet depots, landlords and charging-site operators with contracted uptime promises
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Evidence capture, eligibility determination, claim filing and credit reconciliation for a success fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The site owner or fleet pays after the CPO or OEM issues a verified service credit
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A charger is unavailable or a contracted session fails beyond an SLA allowance

founder_fit: Can validate with a small site portfolio
risks: CPO refusal to accept third-party evidence

structure.control_point: The independently timestamped uptime evidence and invoice-level credit reconciliation
structure.critical_dependency: Contracts must contain enforceable credits and data must distinguish charger failure from vehicle, network and user causes

thesis: For fleet depots and charging-site portfolios, independently reconcile charger availability, successful sessions, field-service records and the CPO or OEM contract. When a service-level failure qualifies, produce the claim packet and match the eventual credit to the invoice. Charge on accepted credits, distributed through charging installers, fleet lessors and energy-service firms; the accepted and rejected claims become a charger reliability and contract-enforceability asset.
title: EV Chargepoint SLA Credit Recovery
